records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb update/create coerce a missing visible param to false, silently flipping group visibility on partial updates
records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, visibility is always reassigned via `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` with no presence check. If a client performs a partial update without sending `visible`, `params[:visible]` is nil and the expression becomes false, silently flipping an existing visible group to invisible. records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members takes limit from user params with no upper bound, allowing the entire membership to be serialized
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) and then used in `.limit(limit)` with no maximum cap. This allows a requester to set an arbitrarily large limit and force serialization of a very large membership list (`serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer)`), which is a performance/DoS risk exposed by this diff.

records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members passes a negative offset through unvalidated to .offset(), producing a SQL error
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no validation/clamping to `>= 0`, so a request with a negative `offset` (e.g. `?offset=-10`) will pass a negative value to ActiveRecord `.offset()`, which can raise an error.

records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") assuming a String, so array-form params raise NoMethodError and return 500 instead of 400
records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. That will raise `NoMethodError` if the incoming `usernames` param is an Array (a common alternative encoding for multi-values), leading to a 500 rather than a handled client error. The diff shows no type-checking/coercion or rescue around this.
